title: Exercise 7B · Q4
summary: The height up the wall is a shorter side — subtract the squares.
alt: Exercise 7B · Q4: A ladder of length 5 m is placed against a vertical wall with its foot 1.8 m away from the base of the wall. How far up the wall does the ladder reach?

hyp.label: Hypotenuse
hyp.text: The side opposite the right angle. It is always the longest side.

legA.label: Shorter side 1
legA.text: One of the two sides that meet at the right angle.

legB.label: Shorter side 2
legB.text: The other side that meets at the right angle.

steps.title: The question
steps.narration: A ladder **AF** of length **5 m** is placed against a vertical wall with its foot **F**, **1.8 m** from the base **C** of the wall. **∠C = 90°**. How far up the wall does the ladder reach (**AC**)?

steps.title: Spot the right angle
steps.narration: In ΔACF, **∠C = 90°**, so the **hypotenuse** is the side opposite it: **AF**. The other two sides meet at the right angle.

steps.title: Pythagoras' theorem
steps.narration: **Pythagoras' theorem**: the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{AF^2} &= \role{legA}{CF^2} + \role{legB}{AC^2}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Make the unknown the subject
steps.narration: We want a **shorter side**, so subtract the known square from the hypotenuse square.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{AF^2} &= \role{legA}{CF^2} + \role{legB}{AC^2} \\ \role{legB}{AC^2} &= \role{hyp}{AF^2} - \role{legA}{CF^2}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Substitute the lengths
steps.narration: Replace each side by its length.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{AF^2} &= \role{legA}{CF^2} + \role{legB}{AC^2} \\ \role{legB}{AC^2} &= \role{hyp}{AF^2} - \role{legA}{CF^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{5^2} - \role{legA}{1.8^2}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Square root
steps.narration: 21.76 is not a perfect square, so use a calculator and round to 3 significant figures.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{AF^2} &= \role{legA}{CF^2} + \role{legB}{AC^2} \\ \role{legB}{AC^2} &= \role{hyp}{AF^2} - \role{legA}{CF^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{5^2} - \role{legA}{1.8^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{25} - \role{legA}{3.24} \\ &= \role{legB}{21.76} \\ \role{legB}{AC} &= \sqrt{21.76} = \role{ans}{4.66\ \text{m}}\end{aligned}\]

formulas.title: Pythagoras' theorem
formulas.text: In a right-angled triangle, the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.

formulas.title: Finding the hypotenuse
formulas.text: Add the two squares, then take the square root.

formulas.title: Finding a shorter side
formulas.text: Subtract the known shorter side's square from the hypotenuse's square, then take the square root.

challenges.title: Now you try
challenges.prompt: A right-angled triangle has hypotenuse **13 m** and one shorter side **5 m**. Find the other shorter side.

takeaways: Find the **right angle** first — the side opposite it is the **hypotenuse**.
To find a shorter side: **subtract** the known shorter side's square from the hypotenuse's square, then take the **square root**.
A shorter side must be **smaller** than the hypotenuse — a quick check on your answer.

notes.title: Exam tip
notes.text: Always begin with a line such as "In ΔABC, ∠C = 90°. Using Pythagoras' Theorem," — it shows which triangle and which right angle you are using.

notes.title: Rounding
notes.text: If the answer is not a whole number, give it to **3 significant figures** unless the question says otherwise.
